title: Community Services budget plan, accessibility and neighbourhood supports
subtitle: Skate park funding, City Centre lease renewal, neighbourhood initiatives policy, and a notice of motion on provincial-municipal finances
overview: Council heard the Community Services 2024-2026 business plan, covering recreation, parks, facilities, fire rescue and municipal enforcement. It was presented ahead of budget day, so no budget decisions were made. Staff outlined optional budget items Council can consider then, including more sidewalk snow clearing and deferring part of the fire master plan expansion. A resident also urged Council to prioritize and stage the proposed tax increase.

Council approved the release of 2024 capital funding for the Neighbourhood Action Sports Parks project, which supports the RIM Park skate park {{vote:m5}}. It adopted the Supporting Neighbourhood-Led Initiatives Policy {{vote:m4}} and approved a lease renewal at the Waterloo City Centre {{vote:m1}}. Council also received the annual facility accessibility update {{vote:m3}} and the neighbourhood strategy report {{vote:m2}}.

For residents, the decisions mean continued support for neighbourhood groups, steady work on making City buildings accessible, and new skate park investment. A notice of motion was tabled asking the province to review municipal finances with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario. Council will consider it on January 29.

decisions.detail: Council approved release of 2024 capital funding of $796,000 for the Neighbourhood Action Sports Parks project, drawn from the Parkland Dedication and Development Charges reserve funds.
Council approved report COM2024-004 and adopted the Supporting Neighbourhood-Led Initiatives Policy (M-016).
Council approved the lease renewal for Raymond James Ltd. and authorized the Mayor and Clerk to sign the amending agreement.
Council received the 2023 annual update on accessibility improvements at City-owned facilities as information.
Council received the report on neighbourhood strategy implementation and supports in 2023 as information.

debate: Councillors asked about the Community Services plan's staffing and programming requests, including an inclusion coordinator, funding for a community youth organization, and permanent versus contract positions. Staff linked these to service needs and to retaining staff.

On fire services, a councillor raised procurement delays for trucks. Staff said pumper lead times have grown from about nine months to about two years, so requested staff could be used flexibly across equipment. Another councillor asked about dispatch costs and whether to bring dispatch in-house. Staff said a regional centre is considered the most cost-efficient option.

A resident delegate said the proposed multi-year tax increase was very high compared with past increases and inflation. The delegate urged Council to prioritize and stage items in the strategic plan and to consider efficiencies, including a review of fire station locations.

Several councillors stressed cost control: reusing park, splash pad and library designs, bundling procurement, and avoiding budgets built on rough estimates. Staff said reuse is possible for simple elements but site conditions can limit it.

On accessibility, councillors asked how the priority matrix weights health, safety and human rights against grants and cost. Staff said those factors score highest and that staff discretion and a review committee also apply. A councillor asked whether the skate park site could also host basketball; staff said the site is constrained but will look at the wider RIM Park site.
